Connecticut

5 directory entries · Research in progress

  • Lenape↗Historical homeland connection
    Connection & source
    Historical homeland connection

    Nation's overview names parts of Connecticut. Not statewide territory.

    Ancestral geography; community account. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Mashantucket Pequot↗Nation published historical community connection
    Connection & source
    Nation published historical community connection

    The Nation's history describes Connecticut colonial grants and the Mashantucket community's return to its original land. Only a Connecticut connection is indexed, without reproducing acreage or treating colonial grants as the origin of Pequot rights.

    Public content inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Mohegan↗Present community and government location
    Connection & source
    Present community and government location

    The Mohegan Tribe's Sachem Uncas page explicitly identifies its reservation in southeastern Connecticut. Only this geographical statement is used here, not the page's interpretation of seventeenth-century alliances. Mohegan is not treated as interchangeable with Mohican or Pequot.

    Current tribal-site geography statement inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Pequot↗Specific descendant government within broader people entry
    Connection & source
    Specific descendant government within broader people entry

    The Nation situates its Pequot history and Mashantucket community in Connecticut. This supplies one Pequot descendant-government connection and does not equate all Pequot communities with Mashantucket.

    Public content inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Quiripi↗Historical language community geography
    Connection & source
    Historical language community geography

    Costa locates Quiripi in southwestern Connecticut, including the Branford mission context of Pierson’s seventeenth-century catechism. Quiripi is a language-related access label, not one government. The study also stresses uncertainty and dialect mixing in the records; language-documentation gaps do not establish disappearance of peoples. Inspection: Actual introduction, printed pp81–83, and Quiripi section, pp116–118. Remaining linguistic analyses were not fully reviewed.

    Seventeenth-century documentation analyzed in a 2007 linguistic study. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗

These are starting lists, not a complete census. Modern borders help you navigate; they are not Indigenous homeland boundaries. A connection may be historical or present-day and does not imply presence throughout a region. Directory names can overlap; the profiles explain their relationships.
